detail.longDescription: I'm running the latest versions of Python and Ruby under Debian Linux version 13. I make use of text preprocessing both in Python and Ruby, and this is only used for preprocessing text in files that are external to Python and Ruby, and it's never used for preprocessing any code within my Python and Ruby programs themselves. Because some of these external text files are read by one or more of my Python programs and also one or more of my Ruby programs, I need to use the same templating language for the preprocessing directives that are used in all of these external text files. Furthermore, I never want to have to shell out to run a preprocessing executable, but rather, I only want to perform the preprocessing via an imported Python package and an imported Ruby package. Therefore, I need to use a templating package that has versions which are importable into Python programs and also which are importable into Ruby programs. The only preprocessor that I've found so far which offers a version that can be imported both into Python code and into Ruby code is Mustache (and some of its 3rd-party forks). But Mustache is limited in that it doesn't offer constructs such as looping and conditional logic. Therefore, I'm looking for alternatives to Mustache which are importable as a Python package and also as a Ruby package. I've investigated m4, cpp, gpp text preprocessor, Mozilla preprocessor, jinja2, filepp, cheetah, and several others, but so far, none that I've found offer all of the capabilities that I've described here. Does anyone know of any Mustache alternatives which fit all of my criteria?
